description: Capability `co-managed-seat` is registered on `release-v2-0-feature`: admission requires the flag and a pool entitlement row for a `psa` tenant; service requires any seat arrangement row; it is included in the server capability bootstrap.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: `FORCE_CAPABILITIES=co-managed-seat:off` closes seat admission and service for every tenant without changing `co-managed`; `co-managed-seat:on` admits without PostHog.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: `co_managed_allocations` carries `allocation_kind` (`workspace` by default, or `seat`) and `sponsor_client_id`; kind-aware constraints require a customer tenant and relationship for workspace rows and a client with neither for seat rows; existing rows read as workspace with no data change.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: One capacity function returns purchased, allocated, available and a per-kind breakdown for a sponsor, and the entitlement, purchase and reservation code paths all use it.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: Reserving and activating a seat-kind allocation for a client is one idempotent command (operation id and request fingerprint) under the entitlement lock; a replay returns the original result.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: A seat-kind reservation is refused with a specific reason when available capacity is insufficient, when the sponsor is not eligible, or while the pool is in lapse grace or read-only.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: A client holds at most one live allocation of either kind; a second request for the same client is refused and names the existing arrangement's shape.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: A seat allocation's seat count can be raised within available capacity and lowered no further than its committed seats.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: Releasing a seat allocation returns its seats to the pool exactly once; a replay is a no-op.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: A pool purchase that would lower capacity below seats allocated across both kinds is refused.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: Pool lapse (capacity below allocated) starts grace and then read-only using seats of both kinds, and a seat allocation follows the same deadline as a workspace allocation.
prdRefs: Segment A — Seat pool: allocation kinds and capability

description: Seat arrangement, board scope, seat assignment and project grant tables exist in the sponsor tenant with tenant-first keys, no triggers, and are registered in the tenant table manifest for deletion and export.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: Creating a seat arrangement for a client reserves and activates its allocation and writes the arrangement in one transaction; a repeated request returns the same arrangement.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: Arrangement creation is refused for an inactive client and for a client that already has a live workspace relationship or seat arrangement.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: An MSP administrator sets which boards are in an arrangement's scope and whether technicians may create tickets on each; an empty scope gives technicians no ticket access.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: An MSP administrator invites a seat technician by name and email for an arrangement; the assignment is recorded as invited and counts as a committed seat; an email already claimed by an internal user elsewhere is refused with that reason.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: An invitation is refused when committed seats would exceed the allocation, and concurrent invitations for the last seat produce exactly one success.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: Accepting the invitation creates an internal user with the seat role and activates the assignment.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: A seat role with operational permissions and no sales, billing, accounting, settings or user-administration permission is seeded for a tenant when its first seat arrangement is admitted; its catalog entries carry the `co-managed-seat` capability and are hidden for tenants not served.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: One function counts the MSP's licensed internal users and excludes users with a live seat assignment; the seat guard, the licence usage figures, the seat-reduction check, onboarding and the appliance seat check all use it.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: Creating, inviting, reactivating or directory-provisioning a seat technician is admitted against the arrangement's allocation and never against the MSP's licensed seat limit.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: Revoking a seat assignment deactivates the user, removes access on the next request and frees the committed seat; it never leaves an ordinary internal user behind.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: Converting a seat technician into an MSP user is an explicit action that passes MSP seat admission, ends the seat assignment and replaces the seat role.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: A user with a live seat assignment can hold only seat roles; assigning another role or adding them to an MSP team is refused.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: Seat admission takes locks in the established order (entitlement, then arrangement) and cannot deadlock against reservation, purchase or hosted reconcile running concurrently.
prdRefs: Segment B — Arrangement, seat assignment and licensing

description: The co-managed package registers a built-in rule resolver for seat subjects: own client on every client-owned resource, in-scope boards for tickets, shared projects for projects, client-visible only for documents, and a closed baseline; the rules are not editable.
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: A seat subject's client, board scope and project grants are resolved from the assignment and arrangement rows on every request, so a change takes effect on the next request with no sign-out.
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: A contract test fails when a resource type in the kernel catalog is neither named by the seat resolver nor listed as denied for seat subjects.
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: Routes, menu sections and product guards resolve per principal: a seat technician gets the operational surface (tickets, projects, devices, documents, time), and every other MSP route answers not found for them.
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: A seat technician cannot create an API key, and REST and MCP requests from a seat principal are refused.
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: Service catalog and eligible contract-line lookups require an internal user with the relevant permission, so neither a seat technician nor a portal user can read services, rates or contract lines.
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: Client records read by a subject without billing permission omit billing columns (payment terms, billing cycle, credit limit, invoicing settings).
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: A seat technician's user lists, pickers and mention suggestions contain MSP staff who participate on tickets they can see (name and avatar only), technicians of their own client, and their client's contacts; no other user of the tenant.
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: A tenant not served by `co-managed-seat` runs zero additional queries on native ticket list, ticket detail, comment write and time-entry paths, recorded as query-budget entries.
prdRefs: Segment C — Seat authority and surface

description: Comment audience visibility is decided by the reader's organization (MSP staff, the ticket client's seat technicians, or requester) through one predicate with a matching SQL form, used by every reader; a seat technician's organization comes from the seat assignment.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: A `shared_it` thread on a ticket of a client with a live seat arrangement is visible to MSP staff and that client's seat technicians and to no requester.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: An `organization_private` thread is visible to MSP staff only.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: A legacy internal thread with no stored audience is never visible to a seat technician and is never treated as shared.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: MSP staff can post a `shared_it` comment through the native comment writer on a ticket of a client with a live seat arrangement; on any other ticket the request is refused.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: A seat technician can post `requester` and `shared_it` comments; `organization_private` and the legacy internal note are refused for them.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: A reply inherits its thread's audience for both organizations.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: Only MSP staff can change a thread's audience, and widening it requires an explicit disclosure confirmation.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: Attachments and inline images are readable by a seat technician only when their parent comment's audience is visible to them.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: Ticket activity and audit entries shown to a seat technician omit events about private notes.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: Search indexing and its access check carry the audience, so a seat technician's search never returns private note text.
prdRefs: Segment D — Conversation audiences by organization

description: The native ticket list offers a seat technician Client IT, With MSP, Unassigned and All views, and each view's count equals the rows its filter returns.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: A seat technician opens a ticket on the native ticket screen with a capability set that turns off billing, quick invoice, materials, credentials, bundles, delete, duplicate, email logs, surveys, scheduling, templates, workflows and category creation.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: The ticket page's server preloads (billing rollup, materials, surveys, email logs and the other capability-gated reads) are skipped when the viewer's capability is off, so those reads are not made for a seat technician.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: The billing profile picker and its change action are absent for a viewer without the billing capability.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: A seat technician creates a ticket only for their own client, on a board that allows creation, with a contact of their own client; responsibility starts with client IT.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: A seat technician edits a ticket's native fields but cannot change its client or move it to an out-of-scope board.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: A seat technician assigns a ticket to themselves or another technician of their client; their assignee picker lists no MSP user.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: The human-work assignee guard refuses assigning a seat technician to a ticket, task or other work item that is not of their own client and in scope.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: A ticket of a client with a live seat arrangement has a responsibility of `client_it` or `msp`; it defaults to `msp` for existing and MSP-created tickets.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: A seat technician hands a ticket to the MSP with a required shared note; responsibility becomes `msp`, the technician assignee is cleared, the arrangement's handoff defaults apply, and a receipt is stored; a replay returns the original receipt.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: MSP staff hand a ticket to client IT with a required shared note and an optional named technician; responsibility becomes `client_it` and a receipt is stored; the request is refused when the ticket's board is out of scope.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: A handoff carries the expected revision and is refused when another handoff or reassignment has intervened.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: On the native ticket screen for a client with a live seat arrangement, MSP staff see who is responsible and a Hand to client IT action; both are absent for every other client.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: The MSP assignee picker lists the ticket client's seat technicians in a separate Client IT group, only on that client's tickets, and never on other clients' tickets.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: The MSP ticket composer offers Requester, Shared IT and Private in place of the Internal toggle for clients with a live seat arrangement, defaulting to Private.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: The seat technician's composer offers Requester and Shared IT and shows each comment's audience.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: The MSP ticket list offers a responsibility filter and column for tenants served by the capability.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: MSP SLA timers pause while a ticket's responsibility is with client IT and resume when it returns, through the ticket lifecycle hooks; tickets of other clients are unaffected.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: Bulk Hand to client IT and bulk Hand to MSP validate each selected ticket separately and report each failure without acting on tickets that do not qualify.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: A seat technician applies existing tags and cannot create a tag.
prdRefs: Segment E — Ticket work and handoff

description: The time-entry dialog opens for a seat technician in operational mode without reading the service catalog, tax or contract data, and saves without running billing allocation.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician's time entry is stored as operational with no service, no contract line and zero billable duration.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: Seat technician time entries never appear in billing runs, invoice previews, unbilled-time lists or timesheet approval queues.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician sees client IT's total effort and their own entries on a ticket; the MSP's total is shown only when the arrangement setting allows it, and MSP staff see both totals.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician lists, edits and deletes their own operational entries; timesheet submission surfaces are absent for them.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: An MSP administrator shares individual projects of the client with the arrangement, and a seat technician sees only shared projects.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician opens a shared project on the native project screen without budget, billing or rate data, and the task form loads without the service catalog.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician updates a task's status, assigns it to a technician of their client, comments with an audience, and logs operational time on it.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician lists and opens their own client's assets with RMM inventory fields, read-only, without billing profile or purchase cost, and with no remote or script action available.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician links one of their client's assets to a visible ticket and creates a ticket from an asset.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician reads client-visible documents of their own client and documents attached to visible tickets, and uploads ticket attachments.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A seat technician reads only knowledge base articles with a client or public audience; internal-audience articles are hidden from them.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: Stored credentials are unavailable to seat technicians on every path.
prdRefs: Segment F — Time, projects, devices and documents

description: A handoff to client IT notifies the named technician, or every active technician of that client when none is named; a handoff to the MSP notifies MSP staff by the existing assignment and board rules.
prdRefs: Segment G — Notifications and email

description: Email and in-app notifications sent to a seat technician contain only content their audience can see, and no notification about a private note is sent to them.
prdRefs: Segment G — Notifications and email

description: A shared IT note notifies the other organization's participants on the ticket.
prdRefs: Segment G — Notifications and email

description: A seat technician's email reply to a shared IT notification is stored as shared IT, and a reply to a requester-audience notification is stored as requester.
prdRefs: Segment G — Notifications and email

description: A seat technician can be added as a watcher on any ticket, like any other address. On a ticket outside their scope they are treated as an external party: they receive only requester-audience content in the client rendering, never MSP links, internal or private notes, and their email replies are stored as requester. On a ticket inside their scope they receive what their audience can see. A ticket moving into or out of their scope changes what an existing subscription delivers, from live rows at delivery time.
prdRefs: Segment G — Notifications and email

description: On a client with no arrangement, the Co-managed IT tab offers Seat and Workspace with one line each, the pool's available seats and any eligibility blocker; choosing Workspace continues into the existing provisioning flow unchanged.
prdRefs: Segment H — MSP administration surfaces

description: The seat arrangement panel shows seats used and allocated and lets an administrator change the allocation, invite, resend and revoke technicians, edit board scope, share projects and set handoff defaults.
prdRefs: Segment H — MSP administration surfaces

description: The Co-managed IT overview lists arrangements of both shapes in one table with client, shape, state and seats used and allocated, alongside pool totals.
prdRefs: Segment H — MSP administration surfaces

description: When available capacity is short, the panel offers the existing pool purchase review for the new pool total and then completes the allocation without a second charge.
prdRefs: Segment H — MSP administration surfaces

description: User administration lists seat technicians apart from MSP staff, labelled with their client, and the licence usage figure excludes them.
prdRefs: Segment H — MSP administration surfaces

description: An administrator can see, for a seat technician and a ticket, why access is or is not granted, using the authorization simulator's reasons.
prdRefs: Segment H — MSP administration surfaces

description: Every seat entry point is contributed through UI slots and gated by `useCapability('co-managed-seat')`, never by the raw flag.
prdRefs: Segment H — MSP administration surfaces

description: Ending a seat arrangement, after a confirmation that lists the effects, deactivates its technicians, releases the allocation once, returns responsibility for its tickets to the MSP and keeps shared notes readable by MSP staff.
prdRefs: Segment I — Ending, lapse and client lifecycle

description: After lapse grace expires, a seat technician's writes are refused with the lifecycle error while sign-in and reads continue, and MSP users and requesters are unaffected.
prdRefs: Segment I — Ending, lapse and client lifecycle

description: Deleting, merging or inactivating a client with a live seat arrangement is refused with a reason, and the arrangement tables are classified in the client-owned table roster.
prdRefs: Segment I — Ending, lapse and client lifecycle

description: Changing a ticket's client, or moving it to an out-of-scope board, clears a seat technician assignee, returns responsibility to the MSP and removes the technician's access, keeping the shared notes.
prdRefs: Segment I — Ending, lapse and client lifecycle

description: A deactivated seat technician can be reactivated only into a live assignment with a free seat.
prdRefs: Segment I — Ending, lapse and client lifecycle
